correctness.rationale: Positive diagonal conjugation makes movement symmetric while keeping seasonal reproductions diagonal. The two-season monodromy is similar to A(d)^T A(d); the induced 2-norm is convex in the affine rate, proving a bound for every dimension and endpoints. A column-sum induced 1-norm proves one-season endpoint optimality. For the three-season example, exact monodromies have radii 4,25/4,4. The two-site mortality transition follows from endpoint eigenvalues and strict triangle-equality incompatibility at the tie; no finite enumeration is used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison against the full-access 2010 period-two evolutionary dispersal paper and 2013 spectral ordering paper found different stated targets and stronger/unrelated assumptions; seven focused published-finding corpus searches found no implication-equivalent result. The proof specializes classical operator-norm convexity to a nontrivial periodic-population growth bound and exhibits a sharp three-season obstruction. Priority remains uncertain due to alternate terminology and inaccessible historical texts.
residual_risks: Operator-norm convexity is elementary and may have been explicitly applied to this ecological objective elsewhere under a matrix-product formulation.
Full text of Hardin–Takáč–Webb (1988) and some source-adjacent comparisons was not accessible; neither is declared NOT_COVERING.
No exhaustive literature-search or independent priority certification; coverage by uninspected primary literature is possible.

value.rationale: Alternating habitat fitness makes dispersal optimization ecologically motivated. The structural endpoint theorem for arbitrary habitat number and unequal reproduction matrices, plus minimal-period counterexample and an exact dispersal-mortality switch, resolve a natural temporal boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. Practical caveats about nonlinear persistence and variable migration are explicitly limited.
